internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root krh is centered on aversion / unwillingness: to find something contrary to one's will or liking. The Quran anchors this with explicit opposites — it is the antonym of ḥubb (love), ṭawʿ (willing submission), and riḍwān (good-pleasure). The same nucleus is re-pointed by morphology: Form II 'makes something detestable' (49:7, paired with 'made beloved'), and Form IV / ikrāh 'compels' someone to act against that aversion (10:99 forcing faith, 24:33 forcing girls, 16:106 the compelled tongue with a heart still at peace, 2:256 'no compulsion in religion'). Aversion is shown to be evaluatively neutral (one may be averse to what is good, 2:216), inner-only (people act while averse, 9:54), and impotent against God's decree ('even though the disbelievers are averse'). The one place the account breaks is 46:15, where a mother bears and delivers her child 'kurhan' — hardship/travail, not aversion — which the Quran never internally equates with the aversion sense.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: krh does NOT entail: (1) hostility/enmity/waging war — it is set against ḥubb and riḍwān, not a term for aggression, which gets separate verbs (61:8 'yurīdūna li-yuṭfiʾū'); (2) a verdict on the object's real worth — one may be averse to what is genuinely good (2:216 't, akrahū shayʾan wa-huwa khayrun lakum'; 4:19); (3) power to prevent the outcome — the 'wa-law kariha' formula makes human aversion inert against the decree; (4) refusal/abstention from the act — aversion coexists with compliance (9:54 spending while averse; ṭawʿan wa-karhan); (5) for Form IV, inner assent — compulsion touches only the outward act, never the heart (16:106, 2:256); (6) agent-side location of the emotion in Form IV — the averse party is the patient, not the compelling subject. And crucially krh does NOT lexically cover experienced hardship/travail with no object of aversion and no coercer (46:15).
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: 46:15 'حَمَلَتْهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرْهًا وَوَضَعَتْهُ كُرْهًا': the mother is honored (the verse grounds a command of iḥsān to parents) and is not averse to the child, so kurhan here rides an axis of experienced hardship/travail that is orthogonal to like/dislike and to against-will; there is no object of aversion, no ṭawʿ-contrast, and no coercer. The Quran nowhere internally equates this kurh-as-hardship with krh-as-aversion, so it is NOT bridged to the aversion nucleus and blocks a single all-41 root generalization.
internal_discovery.strongest_competitor: Two weakly-bridged lexemes on one skeleton: (A) an aversion lexeme (Form I family, kārih, makrūh, karraha, kurh-of-2:216) and (B) a coercion lexeme (Form IV akraha + ikrāh + adverbial karh 'by force'). Its force: no single verse pairs stative kariha with Form IV akraha, and Form IV is not the morphological causative of Form I (Form II is), so the 'dislike → forcing' link is inferred rather than textually enacted, and the aversion vs coercion corpora are near-disjoint. It is rejected as the primary account because the adverbial karh (ṭawʿan wa-karhan) is itself a Form-I noun already meaning 'non-voluntary', which is the exact hinge between disposition and coercion; 4:19 and 2:216 co-locate the poles in one verse; and 16:106/24:33 define the compulsion against the victim's own contrary will. The bridge is therefore corpus-visible, keeping A and B one derivational family — but the strength stops short of UNIVERSAL precisely because this bridge is inferential and 46:15 resists.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form I stative kariha/yakrahu: a subject experiences X as against-inclination — be averse to / disfavor / reject. Object-anchored to God's revelation (47:9, 47:26), His riḍwān (47:28), a task (9:81), persons/acts (4:19:25, 49:12), or elided in the impotent-aversion formula 'wa-law kariha' (10:82, 8:8, 40:14, 9:32, 9:33, 61:8, 61:9). God is a licit subject and there aversion is efficacious (9:46 kariha → fa-thabbaṭahum).

clusters.supporting_evidence_note: 17:38 'كَانَ سَيِّئُهُۥ عِندَ رَبِّكَ مَكْرُوهًا': with God as implied experiencer, makrūhan functions as a normative verdict ('detested in your Lord's sight'), the node where subject-relative aversion coincides with the objective standard; this does not break the aversion nucleus but marks its evaluative edge.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Form II karraha: factitive/causative of aversion — 'make X detestable to someone', explicitly the argument-mirror of ḥabbaba 'made beloved'.
clusters.classification_rationale: Form II causative of the Form-I aversion attitude; the true morphological causative, locking the nucleus to the ḥubb axis.

clusters.candidate_semantic_interpretation: Masdar ikrāh (N of Form IV): 'compulsion / coercion'. 2:256 'lā ikrāha fī l-dīn'; 24:33 'min baʿdi ikrāhihinna'.
clusters.classification_rationale: Verbal-noun of Form IV; nominalizes the coercion branch of the nucleus.

reconciliation.rationale: When the experiencer is God, subject-relative aversion coincides with the objective standard; the object-side passive participle still names the detested thing, so it sits at the nucleus's evaluative edge rather than outside it.

independent_verification: Three independent lenses (A bottom-up, B build, C adversarial) each read all 41/41 tokens and converged on a strong aversion core plus the 46:15 kurh=hardship resistance; adversary C explicitly recommended against a single all-41 nucleus, which this payload honors by scoping to the family and excluding 46:15.
candidate_root_contribution: krh marks the disfavored / against-the-grain-of-the-will pole: an object, act or condition registered as CONTRARY to a self's inclination or acceptance. This nucleus is realized across a coherent derivational family: Form I kariha / active participle kārih = a subject holds the aversion (the averse one); passive participle makrūh = the dispreferred object; Form II karraha = instill the aversion (make detestable, mirror of ḥabbaba); Form IV akraha / masdar ikrāh + adverbial karh = place a person in the against-will condition, i.e. compel to act against inclination. The nucleus is fixed Quran-internally by its own antonyms (ḥubb 2:216/49:7/49:12; ṭawʿ 13:15/3:83/41:11/9:53; riḍwān 47:28) and the compulsion branch is bridged by 16:106 and 24:33. It does NOT extend to the ḍamma-noun kurh of 46:15 (hardship/travail), which is not internally bridged to aversion.

layer_attribution.occurrence_evidence: 41/41 tokens read from krh.json with real Tanzil verse_text and QAC morphology; antonym anchors observed in-verse (2:216 takrahū↔tuḥibbū; 49:7 karraha↔ḥabbaba; 47:28 kariha↔riḍwān; 13:15/3:83/41:11/9:53 karh↔ṭawʿ) and the compulsion frame (agent+person+ʿalā) in 20:73/24:33.
layer_attribution.derivation: Morphology systematically re-points one nucleus: Form I / participles = hold the aversion; Form II karraha = instill it (causative, mirror of ḥabbaba); Form IV akraha + masdar ikrāh + adverbial karh = place a person in the against-will condition (compel). Form IV is the semantic (not strict morphological) causative bridged via the non-voluntary noun karh.

layer_attribution.contextual_relation: Narrative/legal contexts (disbelievers averse to revelation; forcing faith/prostitution/magic; inheritance by force; spending while averse; God's disfavor holding back the hypocrites) supply intensity and object but are held OUT of the root claim; the 'wa-law kariha' polemical formula and the iḥsān-to-parents frame of 46:15 are contextual, not the nucleus.
layer_attribution.reconciliation: 17:38 (subjective→normative with God as experiencer) and 2:216:5:1 (ḍamma kurh sharing vocalization with resistant 46:15) were reconciled to CONSISTENT because each is anchored in-verse to the aversion nucleus (God-as-experiencer object of detestation; kurh bound to takrahū on one object).

rejection_condition.challenging_finding: A Quranic occurrence in which Form IV akraha/ikrāh denotes an inner emotional aversion (not imposition of an outward act on a patient), OR a Form I kariha/kārih that denotes compelling a person rather than an experiencer's aversion — i.e. the experiencer↔agent argument-role split that seals the aversion and coercion branches is violated within the corpus.
rejection_condition.search_location: The Form IV / masdar tokens (10:99:11:1, 16:106:9:1, 20:73:8:1, 24:33:29:1, 24:33:41:1, 2:256:2:1, 24:33:46:1) checked against the Form I / participle tokens (2:216:9:1, 4:19:25:1, 49:12:25:2, the kārih tokens) for argument frame and locus of the averse party.
rejection_condition.verification_method: Re-read each token's verse_text and qac_verb_form; confirm Form IV always takes agent + person-object (+ ʿalā act) with the aversion, if any, in the patient (16:106, 24:33), and Form I always takes an experiencer-subject registering an object.
rejection_condition.confounder_control: Distinguish the adverbial karh 'by force' (Form-I noun, 13:15/3:83/41:11/9:53/4:19:10) from Form IV verbal coercion so that the non-voluntary noun is not miscounted as evidence that Form I itself means 'compel'; keep the ḍamma kurh (2:216 vs 46:15) vocalically separated.
rejection_condition.failure_consequence: If such a role-flip occurs, the derivational-family claim collapses into two unbridged homographic lexemes and the result must be downgraded to UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY (no safe bridge across the aversion and coercion classes).

reopen_conditions: If a Quran-internal warrant is found equating the ḍamma-noun kurh of 46:15 (hardship/travail) with the aversion/against-will nucleus — e.g. another kurh token pairing hardship with an aversion verb or a ṭawʿ-contrast — then 46:15 could be folded in and the scope reconsidered toward UNIVERSAL.

If the ṭawʿ↔karh contrast or the 16:106/24:33 compulsion-against-will bridge is challenged such that the adverbial karh no longer hinges aversion to coercion, reopen to test whether Form IV should split off as an independent coercion lexeme (UNRESOLVED_CLASS_ONLY).
If a new occurrence shows Form I kariha meaning 'compel' or Form IV akraha meaning inner 'dislike', reopen the experiencer↔agent role split that currently seals the two branches.

falsification_evidence.status_rationale: No UNIVERSAL root-wide nucleus is asserted: the claim is REPRESENTATIVE / DERIVATIONAL_FAMILY, and two occurrences (46:15) persist as RESISTANT. Per protocol, when the core holds but some occurrences resist, falsification is NOT_RUN and the resistant refs are recorded in counterevidence_refs and RESISTANT_SEAM hard_cases rather than a PASSED verdict being claimed. Distinctiveness from ḥubb/ṭawʿ/riḍwān/sakhaṭ is corpus-attested and the claim is falsifiable via the argument-role-flip condition.
